observations: The southern court shows two upper rows of paired broad windows. The left straight stair rises towards the gallery. Two open bays have thin metal guards, continuous stone paving and a visible recessed wall.

The brick portal has a radial brick face, four moulded bands, projecting spring blocks and two downward brick tails. The entrance tunnel and its successive red ribs continue beyond the fan stair. The raised wordmark is above the doorway and the four-character sign is inside the slit.

The north elevation retains two gabled wings with circular high vents. The two centre areas carry denser curtains of ivy, while the structural window lines remain identifiable. Leaf distribution and tint are an approximation of the 2018 photograph.

The near roof has individual tile courses, open zinc valleys, a central attic door, the terrace and three stacks. The reduced roof retains the pitches, longitudinal courses, dormer and all three flue groups.

The street and overhead overall cameras were aligned to the actual exported geometry. Both final meshes leave 45 pixels above and below the whole villa in these two views. The detailed portrait shows the spring blocks and stepped vault above the stone stair.
calibration: Ground floor and upper openings derived from Wutopia Lab drawings. Photo comparison uses post-renovation garden and north elevations and two dated east street observations.
authorship: All inspection pictures were rasterized from the independently decoded GLBs and the original embedded metric pebble material. No reference photos are embedded.
